discrepancies.uwp: Native orientation: Landscape; Current orientation: Landscape; Auto-rotation preferences: None
discrepancies.winui: Native orientation: N/A; Current orientation: N/A; Auto-rotation preferences: 'DisplayInformation not available on desktop: Element not found. GetForCurrentView must be called on a thread that is associated with a CoreWindow.'
discrepancies.note: The migrated app uses DisplayInformation.GetForCurrentView(), which throws on WinUI 3 desktop. The sample's primary output (reporting native/current orientation) is non-functional and displays a raw exception message instead of orientation data. A visible fallback exists (non-blank), but the core feature does not work.

discrepancies.uwp: Auto-rotation preferences fits on one line ('None').
discrepancies.winui: The exception fallback text overflows/wraps and is clipped at the window edge.
discrepancies.note: Consequence of the exception message being long; cosmetic relative to the functional defect above.

structural_coverage: 5/5 controls present in WinUI UIA tree
behavioral: Apply preferences button produced no visible text change in BOTH UWP and WinUI (0/1 live in each) — not a regression by itself. The regression is in the orientation OUTPUTS, which are broken in WinUI.
